Major fintech advancements in recent years have attracted the attention of financial regulators around the world, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). HKMA stands ready to embrace technology and innovations that emerge in the course of fintech development. In particular, HKMA adopts a risk-based and technology-neutral approach in its supervision. To achieve that, HKMA emphasizes three key factors: its willingness to learn about and understand fintech; its ability to maintain close contact with the industry and other stakeholders; and its ability to achieve a good balance between market development and customer protection. HKMA also maintains close contact with the industry and regulators in other jurisdictions to ensure the existing regulations are up to date. The most recent fintech developments spearheaded by HKMA include: (1) open application programming interface for banks; (2) faster payment system (FPS) and common QR code standard for retail payments; (3) trade finance initiatives; and (4) virtual banking. HKMA has devoted substantial resources to research and application. Some of the research output has already been adopted and is being used by the industry.

Banking stands at a crossroads shaped by rapid innovation, regulatory pressure, and society’s demand for inclusion and sustainability. The Future of Banking - Innovation, Risk and Inclusion maps this terrain with contributions that connect strategy to execution, showing how technology, governance, and prudence can move in step. The book explains where value is migrating, from AI-driven services and customer-experience analytics to data-sharing platforms, while clarifying what it takes to scale safely. It covers open banking, wallets, and bank–fintech collaboration; the “engine room” of risk and capital (creditworthiness under EBA LOM, AI‑enabled credit scoring, CCR backtesting, and operational risk across developed and emerging markets); and the foundations of trust in governance, ethics, and faith‑based models. Practical levers for inclusion are highlighted through evidence on mobile payments for Generation Z, MSME, and women‑focused credit, and rural fintech delivery, while climate‑related disclosures and green finance complete a roadmap for resilient, responsible banking. Designed for academics, supervisors, and industry leaders, the book provides a clear comparative view of what works, where it falls short, and how to transition from pilots to enterprise adoption, without compromising stability, client responsibility, and measurable impact.

sections.heading: Fintech Development in Hong Kong, China
paragraphs: ### Payment Fintech Funding Doubles in H1 [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] This trend is particularly notable in Hong Kong, where the financial landscape continues to evolve with the rapid advancements in fintech. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been at the forefront of these developments, demonstrating a proactive approach to embracing technology and innovations. [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] HKMA, the regulatory body responsible for overseeing the financial sector, has adopted a risk-based and technology-neutral approach in its supervision. This approach emphasizes three key factors: the willingness to learn about and understand fintech, the ability to maintain close contact with the industry and other stakeholders, and the ability to achieve a good balance between market development and customer protection.

By doing so, HKMA aims to ensure that the financial sector remains resilient and adaptable to the ever-evolving landscape of fintech. [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] To support this approach, HKMA has invested substantial resources in research and application. Some of the research output has already been adopted and is being used by the industry. This includes the development of open application programming interfaces (APIs) for banks, which facilitate smoother integration between different financial systems.

The faster payment system (FPS) and the common QR code standard for retail payments have also been implemented, enhancing the efficiency and accessibility of transactions. Additionally, trade finance initiatives and the promotion of virtual banking have been spearheaded by HKMA, aiming to provide innovative solutions to businesses and consumers. [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] The HKMA’s efforts have been complemented by its close collaboration with regulators in other jurisdictions to ensure that the existing regulations remain up to date. This collaboration ensures that the financial sector remains compliant and protected, even as it continues to innovate and adapt.

[[S2|Econstor Econstor]] ### Fintech Development in Hong Kong, China [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] Fintech development in Hong Kong, China, has been characterized by a series of significant advancements that have attracted the attention of financial regulators worldwide. The rapid growth of fintech companies in the region is driven by several factors, including the large unbanked population and the rise of mobile money and cryptocurrencies. These innovations have provided accessible financial solutions to individuals and informal businesses, particularly those without access to traditional banking systems. [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] The report by PORTO@Iris highlights the importance of fintech in the context of the platformed motorcycle economies in urban Africa.

It emphasizes the financial-inclusion thrust, which links fintech to two-wheel paratransit and the multiple ways in which digital platforms create new financial pathways. The report also underscores the crucial importance of payment gateways as infrastructures for additional data-driven financial innovation, the promises of risk-management through data, and the pilot-based experimental practices that give effect to these promises. [[S2|Econstor Econstor]] The insights provided by this report are particularly relevant for researchers, regulators, and private actors in the field.

sections.heading: FinTech Innovations in Digital Banking
paragraphs: ### Payment Fintech Funding Doubles in H1 [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

This growth is attributed to the expanding market demand for innovative payment solutions and the increasing investment in emerging technologies. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

One of the key drivers of this growth is the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in payment processing. AI-powered payment solutions are designed to enhance security, reduce fraud, and streamline the payment process. For instance, AI algorithms can analyze transaction patterns to detect anomalies and prevent fraud more effectively than traditional methods. This not only improves the security of transactions but also reduces the operational costs for financial institutions. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

Another significant innovation in the payment fintech sector is the integration of augmented reality (AR) technology. AR technology is being used to enhance the customer experience in various industries, including retail, healthcare, and manufacturing. In retail, AR technology is used to provide virtual try-on experiences, allowing customers to see how products would look on them before making a purchase. This not only increases customer satisfaction but also reduces the need for physical store visits, thereby saving time and reducing operational costs. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

Blockchain technology, which was initially introduced in 2018, has also seen a significant increase in funding. Blockchain technology is being used to enhance the security and transparency of financial transactions. For instance, blockchain-based payment solutions are being used to streamline cross-border payments, reducing the time and cost associated with traditional payment methods. This not only improves the efficiency of financial transactions but also reduces the risk of fraud and enhances the security of financial data. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

The increasing investment in blockchain technology is also being driven by the growing demand for secure and transparent financial transactions. As more businesses and consumers embrace blockchain technology, the need for secure and transparent financial transactions is becoming increasingly important. This has led to a significant increase in the funding for blockchain-based payment solutions, which are being used to enhance the security and transparency of financial transactions. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

Overall, the growth in funding for payment fintech companies is a testament to the increasing demand for innovative payment solutions and the increasing investment in emerging technologies. As the market continues to evolve, we can expect to see even more innovative payment solutions and technologies that will continue to transform the way we pay for goods and services. [[S4|International Journal of Engineering Research and]]

sections.heading: Customer Data Access and Fintech Entry: Early Evidence from Open
paragraphs: ### Payment Fintech Funding Doubles in H1 [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] This increase is attributed to various factors, including the growing demand for digital payment solutions and the increasing investment in emerging technologies. [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] Customer data access, a key aspect of fintech, has also seen a surge in adoption. The National Bureau of Economic Research's study on "Customer Data Access and Fintech Entry: Early Evidence from Open Banking" highlights that the implementation of open banking policies has empowered consumers to share their transaction data with fintech companies and other banks. [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] The Open Banking initiative, which allows for the sharing of financial data between banks and fintech companies, has been adopted in 49 countries.

This policy has not only improved consumer trust in fintech companies but has also spurred investment in the sector. The UK microdata further supports this trend, showing that the implementation of open banking policies has enabled consumers to access financial advice and credit, as well as established new fintech lending relationships for SMEs. [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] In a calibrated model, the National Bureau of Economic Research's study on "Customer Data Access and Fintech Entry: Early Evidence from Open Banking" suggests that open banking universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, open banking promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

[[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] The OpenAlex research index, a comprehensive database on Chinese investments in Indonesia's fintech sector, provides insights into the interactions between Chinese investors and the Indonesian government. This research paper analyzes the Chinese investment in Indonesia's fintech sector, focusing on fintech lending, which has become a major source of controversy. It addresses the local debates over the intentions and structure of Chinese investors in the Indonesian fintech sector, comparing them to the actual situation of Chinese FDI in Indonesia. [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] Despite the controversies surrounding Chinese investment in Indonesian fintech, particularly in the payday loan sector, there is insufficient evidence to conclude that the problems with the industry are the result of Chinese investment bringing bad business practices and governance to Indonesia.

Instead, the problems can be explained by the nature of the industry, Indonesia's rapidly expanding middle class, and regulators that must react to problems as they arise rather than controlling innovation to allow the market to meet consumer needs. [[S7|National Bureau of Economic Research]] Indonesia's evolving regulatory governance has played a crucial role in shaping the fintech sector. The Indonesian version of the research paper elaborates on how Chinese investors respond to the evolving regulatory environment in Indonesia and addresses local debates over the intentions and structure of Chinese investors in the Indonesian fintech sector.

sections.heading: Essays on political economy of finance and fintech
paragraphs: ### Payment Fintech Funding Doubles in H1 [[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] This growth is attributed to several factors, including increased interest in the sector, technological advancements, and regulatory support. [[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] The sector has experienced a period of rapid innovation, with new technologies and platforms emerging that are reshaping the way payments are made. This innovation has attracted a growing number of investors, who are seeking out the potential for high returns and the ability to disrupt traditional payment methods. [[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] One of the key drivers of this growth is the increasing recognition of the importance of fintech in driving economic growth and innovation.

Governments around the world are recognizing the potential of fintech to create new jobs, stimulate economic growth, and improve the efficiency of financial services. This recognition has led to a surge in funding for fintech companies, including those focused on payment solutions. [[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] Another factor contributing to the growth in funding for payment fintech companies is the increasing demand for faster and more secure payment methods. With the rise of digital payments and the increasing use of mobile devices, there is a growing need for faster and more secure payment solutions.

This demand has led to a surge in funding for companies focused on developing new payment technologies and solutions. [[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] The regulatory environment has also played a crucial role in driving the growth of funding for payment fintech companies. Governments around the world are implementing new regulations and guidelines to ensure the stability and safety of the financial system. This has led to a surge in funding for companies focused on developing new payment technologies and solutions that comply with these regulations.

[[S2|Data Archiving and Networked Services DANS]] Overall, the growth in funding for payment fintech companies is a reflection of the increasing recognition of the potential of fintech to drive economic growth and innovation. This growth is expected to continue as the sector continues to evolve and as governments and regulators continue to implement new regulations and guidelines to ensure the stability and safety of the financial system.
